sections.notes:
20 UD units are required, distributed as follows
Substitutions and waivers are subject to approval by the program director.

narrative:
Students must consult the General Catalog for prerequisites to required courses.
The following conditions must also be met for official recognition of the minor:
- The sponsoring program reports completion of the minor prior to the posting of the degree.
- At least 18 upper-division quarter units are completed for the minor. (Waivers cannot reduce the requirement below this number.)
- The UC grade-point average in ALL applied upper-division courses is 2.0 or higher.
- No more than 5 upper-division units overlap between this minor and the upper-division portion of the
major(s) or other minor(s). If overlap is greater with the major(s), completion of the minor will not be formally recognized; if overlap with other minor(s) is greater, only the first minor reported will be recognized

nodes.title: Introductory Cultural Anthropology
nodes.description: The nature of culture: survey of the range of cultural phenomena, including material culture, social organization, religion, and other topics.

nodes.title: World Archaeology
nodes.description: An introduction to archaeology and the history of humankind from the earliest times through the advent of literate civilization and cities, also processes of cultural change and the importance of archaeology to people and societies today. Partly self-paced learning.

nodes.title: Introduction to Archaeology
nodes.description: Introduction to archaeology and the prehistory of humankind from the earliest times up to the advent of civilization and cities, also processes of cultural change.

nodes.title: Introductory Biological Anthropology
nodes.description: An introductory course in human evolutionary biology. Natural selection and its genetic basis are used to highlight a variety of human traits. The fossil record is addressed, but the course takes more of an adaptationist than a paleontological perspective.

nodes.title: Introductory Biosocial Anthropology
nodes.description: An introduction to our evolved, universal human nature, the evolution of the human mind, and how they shape behavior, social life, and culture. Topics include friendship, mate choice, incest avoidance, cooperation, revenge, status, jealousy, emotions, group formation, and intergroup aggression.

nodes.title: Basic Archaeological Concepts
nodes.description: A survey of important archaeological methods of excavation, analysis, and interpretation. Focus will be on the problems and promise of various approaches to the explanation of past human behavior.

nodes.title: Indigenous People and the Nation State in the Americas
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: The changing relationship between indigenous people and the state. Compare the differences and similarities between indigenous peoples' mobilizations in the cases of Canada, USA, Ecuador, Chile, Guatemala, Bolivia and Mexico.

nodes.title: Borders and Borderlands
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: The theoretical concept of "borderlands" examined through a discussion of the societies, economics and cultures that form on geopolitical borders. The Mexico-U.S. border will be discussed in detail.

nodes.title: Behavioral Ecology of Hunter Gatherers
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: A thorough introduction using a behavioral ecology approach to the diversity of behaviors found among foragers in Africa, South America, Southeast Asia, and Australia. Topics include: diet and subsistence, mating, demography, social behavior, mobility and settlement patterns, gender, indigenous rights, and conservation.

nodes.title: Cultural Development in Mesoamerica
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: The rise and fall of various ancient civilizations such as those of the Maya, Aztecs, Toltecs, Teotihuacanos, and Olmec as well as their cultural antecedents. This course uses self-paced audiovisual modules as well as traditional lecture format.

nodes.title: Cultural Anthropology of Latin America
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Contemporary issues of rural and urban societies in the Caribbean, and Central and South America. Examination of continuities and changes in cultural institutions and values; inequality, colonialism, settler colonialism, state formation, indigenous social movements, race, gender, class and ethnicity, urbanization, extractivism.

nodes.title: Cultural Anthropology of Mexico
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: An examination of contemporary issues in Mexico through an anthropological lens. Topics may include race, class, gender, and sexuality, nation-state formation, settler colonialism, decolonization, social movements, and political economy.

nodes.title: The Ancient Maya
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: The splendiferous Maya civilization as it waxed and waned during ancient times.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES

nodes.title: The Origins of Complex Societies
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Why and how complex societies developed from simple, egalitarian societies in some areas of the world. Course surveys major theories and evidence surrounding the origins of states and urban societies in New and Old World.

nodes.title: Field Training Archaeology
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Introduction to design of research projects and techniques of data collection in archaeology. The number of units taken in one course will depend on the amount of training and experience received.

nodes.title: Negritude and African Literature
nodes.description: History of Francophone West Indian and African literature from the 1920s through the 1950s. Writers studied include Aime and Suzanne Cesaire, Leon Gontran Damas, Leopold Sedar Senghor, and Jane and Paulette Nardal.

nodes.title: The Black Francophone Novel
nodes.description: A study of theoretical and literary discourses of decolonization that appeared simultaneously in Africa and the West Indies after the second World War. Writers studied include Mongo Beti, Camara Laye, Aime Cesaire, Ferdinand Oyono, Miriam Warner-Viegyra, Maryse Conde, and Simone Schwartz-Bart.

nodes.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
nodes.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

nodes.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
nodes.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

nodes.title: Introduction to Chicano/a Studies
nodes.description: Introduction to the historical and contemporary development of the Chicano/a community. Course is interdisciplinary in nature. Focuses by quarter on A. history, B. gender, and C. culture.

nodes.title: Indigenous People and the Nation State in the Americas
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: The changing relationship between indigenous people and the state. Compare the differences and similarities between indigenous peoples' mobilizations in the cases of Canada, USA, Ecuador, Chile, Guatemala, Bolivia and Mexico.

nodes.title: Critical Race Theory in Chicana/o Education
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Examines Critical Race Theory (CRT) as an emerging analytical framework in the field of education. Course investigates how a CRT framework might address and challenge the impacts of race, class, gender, language, immigrant status, accent, and sexual orientation on Chicana/o, Latina/o educational attainment and achievement.

nodes.title: Chicana/o Mexican Cultural Heritage
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.prereq_text: Chicano Studies 1A or 1B or 1C or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: A panoramic view of present-day Chicana/o traditions analyzed from a Mexican cultural heritage perspective in order to comprehend and appreciate the uniqueness and difference of present-day Chicano/o culture, its achievements, and contribution to the overall American culture.

nodes.title: Central Americans in the United States
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Provides an interdisciplinary historical overview of Central American migrations to the U.S., and a cultural and political analysis of resulting individual and group identities. Transnationalism, diasporas, politics, and community building among Central Americans, or "Central American-Americans" are explored.

nodes.title: The Brown/Black Metropolis: Race, Class, & Resistance in the City
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Traces the transition of Browns/Blacks from a rural urban population and examines trends in family size, language, usage, segregation and social inequality. Issues of urban decay and community conflict are also examined.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES

nodes.title: Global Migration, Transnationalism in Chicana/o Contexts
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: This course considers Chicana/o and U.S. Latina/o culture(s) within the context of transnational practices and patterns including both hemispheric and global migration trajectories.

nodes.title: Survey of Chicano Literature
nodes.description: The course encompasses a general overview of all genres (poetry, novel, theater, short story and essay) of Chicano literature. A people's socio-historical experiences are examined to understand ethnicity, creativity, and world view.

nodes.title: Chicana/o Novels
nodes.description: Reading, analysis and critique of the contemporary Chicano novel as it pertains to the Chicano experience.

nodes.title: Border Narrative
nodes.description: Reading and analysis of U.S./Mexico border narratives (novels, essays, short stories, autobiographies) focusing on the problems associated with relations between countries.

nodes.title: Chicana Writers
nodes.prereq_text: Department approval required to finalize registration.
nodes.description: Examination of literary works by Chicana writers. Feminist theories as well as other contemporary critical theories are applied to the analysis of prose, poetry and dramatic works written by such authors as Sandra Cisneros, Ana Castillo, Helen Viramontes, and others.

nodes.title: Immigration and the U.S. Border
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Immigration and the U.S. border. An analysis of the socioeconomic and political factors which have determined and continue to form the basis for the development of United States immigration policies and practices toward Mexico and the U.S.-Mexican border.

nodes.title: Practicum in Community Based Learning
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Students do practicum hours in the local community and schools, read relevant articles and examine results from related research projects.

nodes.title: Introduction to Environmental Studies
nodes.description: Environmental Studies requires insights from many disciplines, including the social as well as biophysical science and the humanities. This introduction offers an overview of the field, examining both our planet and the ways in which we humans depend on it.

nodes.title: Introduction to Environmental Science
nodes.description: Provides integration of fundamental science with environmental topics. Includes impacts of human population increase; principles of systems and change, biogeochemical cycles, ecosystems and global climate; energy and laws of thermodynamics; water supply and pollution; toxicology and risk analysis; air pollution and stratospheric ozone depletion.

nodes.title: Introduction to the Social and Cultural Environment
nodes.description: An introduction to the relationship of societies and the environment from prehistorical times to the present. The course is global in perspective, and includes history, literature, philosophy, economics, science, and culture as evidence for examining the human social environment.

nodes.title: People, Place, and Environment
nodes.description: Survey of spatial differentiation and organization of human activity and interaction with the Earth's biophysical systems. Sample topics include human spatial decision-making behavior, migration, population growth, economic development, industrial location, urbanization, and human impacts on the natural environment.

nodes.title: Geography of Latin America
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.prereq_text: Geography 5 or Global Studies 1 or 2 or Environmental Studies 1 or 2 or 3.
nodes.description: El Pueblo, a vila, li tenamit: however you call where you live, geography matters. How and why are human and physical patterns inscribed where they are on the Latin American landscape?

nodes.title: Global History, Culture and Ideology
nodes.description: A survey of the historical processes that have brought different areas of the world into closer contact. Topics include ideologies of nationalism, democracy, and liberalism; international trade and migrations; technological changes; colonialism; the globalization of culture; and the reactions to them.

nodes.title: Global Socioeconomic and Political Processes
nodes.description: Examination of contemporary social, economic, political, and environmental change in a global context; the emergence of a global economy and new systems of world order; and the debate over globalization and whether or not it is desireable.

nodes.title: Human Rights and World Order
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: This course will analyze theories, patterns, cases, and causes of human rights violations throughout the world. What are the international human rights standards? What remedies are available at the global, national, social, and individual levels?

nodes.title: Global Ideologies and World Order
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Deals with conceptions of the world as a unitary political system and how these views come into confrontation with one another. Topics include the nation-state system, political ideologies, international organizations, global conflict, and the emergent civil society.

nodes.title: Peace, Conflict, and Violence in Global Perspective
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: What distinguishes a country at peace from one experiencing war? How do we define types of violence, ranging from the interpersonal level to civil conflict, interstate war, and mass atrocities? This course examines theories and empirical studies of conflict and violence from the local to the global, drawing on approaches from across the social sciences. We work to understand individual and collective behavior in conflict and violent environments and how the social, political, and economic factors motivating or facilitating conflict might be altered or addressed to help build more sustainable peace. The course is highly participatory with a mixed structure: one interactive lecture and one session of small group discussions each week.

nodes.title: Global Economy and Development
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Examines recent theories and perspectives on global political economy and development studies. Topics include, among others, the new global economy, transnational corporations, transnational labor markets, international trade and finance, social and economic development, and North-South relations.

nodes.title: The Political Economy of the Globalization of Finance
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: A critical and historical exploration of the economics and politics of finance as they operate on a global scale in the 20th & 21st centuries. Students examine the historical roots, driving forces, consequences, and challenges of financial globalization, delving into how it shapes interactions within domestic economies with a particular focus on developing and emerging economies. Additionally, we examine financialization and its implications for developing and emerging economies. Other topics include financial (de)regulations, the role of global financial institutions, financial power dynamics, the hierarchical structure of the global financial system, and the integration of financial systems on a global scale.

nodes.title: Sexuality and Globalization
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Examines globalizing cultural politics of sexuality through literature, popular media, subaltern performances, and press discourse from Global South; engages questions of universalized LGBTQ identities, Islamic law and sexual rights, militarized masculinities, recognition of transexualities, and queer, anti-racist and feminist globalisms.

nodes.title: Energy in Global Societies
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: The course examines how energy choices are made and investigates our views of nature, society and markets. Students will read both historical and contemporary accounts of energy politics to understand linkages between the global and the local. Students will learn to think critically and creatively about energy.

nodes.title: Latin American History: Pre-Columbian and Colonial Periods
nodes.description: History 8A-B are general survey courses designed to introduce students to major themes in Latin American history. This course focuses on the diverse histories, politics, cultures, and societies of Mesoamerica, South America, and the Caribbean in the pre-Columbian and colonial periods. Topics include indigenous cultures, Mexica (Aztec) and Inca expansion, Spanish and Portuguese invasion, African diaspora, colonialism, law and legal institutions, religious conversion, trade and economic change, and 18th-century reform.

nodes.title: Latin American History: Independence and National Period
nodes.description: History 8A-B are general survey courses designed to introduce students to major themes in Latin American history. This course encompasses the crisis of colonial rule in the late eighteenth century, independence wars in the early nineteenth century, and the birth and transformations of independent republics from Mexico through the Caribbean to the Andes and the Southern Cone, into the twenty-first century. The course emphasizes the diversity of the Latin American experience with special attention to political processes and social transformations including revolutions, slavery and its legacies, and the struggle for citizenship and democracy, with particular attention to the working classes and ingenious movements.

nodes.title: Colonialism and Language
nodes.prereq_text: HIST 8 or HIST 8A or HIST 8B or HIST 151A or 151B or 154LA or 154LB or upper division standing
nodes.description: All colonial projects had to face the problem of linguistic differences. The ways in which they did so varied widely and are very revealing of their different ambitions, ideological foundations, and local circumstances. Explores the history of colonialism comparatively from the perspective of language, from the late fifteenth to the early nineteenth centuries, in the Americas, Africa, and Europe.

nodes.title: Latin American History
nodes.description: A survey on nineteenth-century Latin America. Topics include: the independence movements, the formation of national states, nationalism, liberalism, the construction of race and racial imaginings, slavery and the struggles for citizenship.

nodes.title: Global Blackness: Race, Repair and Reparation
nodes.description: Discusses historical and contemporary conditions of Black and racialized communities living under economic and militarized oppression in a global perspective. Texts, films and lecture presentations foregrounds the critical role of Black subjects in the expansion of global capitalism. Explores current global conditions of Black and racialized communities living under militarized and economic apartheid. Spotlights the role of culture in shaping struggles of Black communities around the world for self-determination, the (im)possibilities of colonial repair and collective demands for reparation.

nodes.title: Survey: Arts of the Ancient Americas
nodes.description: An introduction to select art traditions from Mesoamerica to Andean South America. Examines architecture, ceramics, sculpture, painting and other classes of material culture for their meaning and function within sociopolitical, religious, and economic contexts.

nodes.title: Introduction to Caribbean Studies
nodes.description: A survey of the culture and society of the Caribbean. After surveying Amerindian communities and examining the impact of the Atlantic slave trade, focus will be on slavery, emancipation, African and Creole cultures,and the issues accompanying an independent nationhood status.

nodes.title: Introduction to the Latin American and Iberian World
nodes.description: Introduction to issues debates, and approaches in the study of Latin America, Spain and Portugal, and the Latinx world, from an interdisciplinary perspective. Topics considered include history, culture, society, and literature from various places and times.

nodes.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies
nodes.description: Designed to acquaint students with current research on the main areas of Latin American and Iberian Studies.

nodes.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the History and Societies of Latin America and Iberia
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Issues central to the study of Latin America and Iberia across the social sciences and history. Topics include nationalism, revolution, politics and the state, economic development and international relations, labor, popular culture, race, gender, religion, migration, environment, imperialism, and colonialism.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES

nodes.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the Cultures, Languages, and Literatures of Latin America and Iberia
nodes.description: Issues pertinent to the diverse cultures, languages, and literatures of Latin America and Iberia. Disciplines and approaches may include: pre-Columbian studies, Spanish and Spanish American literatures, Portuguese and Brazilian literatures, translation studies, cultural, gender, and queer studies, romance language and linguistics.

nodes.title: Media, Culture, and Society in Latin America and Iberia
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Introduces students to Latin American theories, practices and representations about the media, analyzing from a cross-cultural and comparative perspective various cultural productions of the Spanish-speaking world that cross the domains of word, image, and sound.

nodes.title: Spanish for Healthcare
nodes.description: Designed for students interested in expanding and applying their knowledge of Spanish to the medical field. Students will learn and apply targeted vocabulary/grammar and develop bicultural/bilingual competency of healthcare issues in Hispanic countries and the US.

nodes.title: The Hispanic Novel and Cinema
nodes.description: Study of three or four Hispanic novels vis-a-vis their film versions, permitting analysis of narrative in both genres, using existing films and videos based on masterpieces of Hispanic literature. Taught in Spanish.

nodes.title: Vanguard Poetry in Spanish America
nodes.description: A survey of the poetry of the Spanish-American avant-guarde focusing on its three main tendencies: colloquial or antipoetic poetry, existentially or politically committed poetry, and self-referential, narcissistic poetry.

nodes.title: Spanish American Women's Writing
nodes.description: An introduction to nineteenth- and twentieth-century Spanish American women's writings. Themes may include women's participation in the formation of national literatures, their engagement with a tradition of women's writing, and issues of authorship and authority.

nodes.title: Global Climate Justice from the South
nodes.description: This online course examines the science, policy, and politics of global climate change with an emphasis on the Global South, and a social science focus on equity and justice. Students will learn directly from expert faculty from across the UC system and beyond. In addition, students will engage with readings and multimedia content to deepen their understanding of the most pressing climate change issues and solutions. Students will be evaluated through a variety of written products (review questions, journal responses, and a final paper) in which they identify connections across seemingly disparate places. Students will gain knowledge and skills needed to identify the larger system changes needed to adequately address the climate crisis.

nodes.title: Language And Linguistics
nodes.description: Introduction to the scientific study of language: The sounds of language; word and sentence structure; semantics and pragmatics; discourse and conversational speech; the social and cultural functions of language; language change and the reconstruction of languages at earlier stages.

nodes.title: Language as Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Views language through the lens of culture, exploring language as a sociocultural system that organizes meaning, memory, interpretation, authority, action, practice. How practices of speaking shape culture; intertextuality; linguistic and cultural relativity; relations between language, thought, and culture.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES

nodes.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
nodes.description: Introduction to the workings of various political systems with an emphasis on governmental institutions and political processes. Comparison of political systems using some of the basic concepts of political analysis.

nodes.title: Introduction to International Relations
nodes.description: An introduction to the basic concepts, theories, and problems of international relations; balance of power, deterrence, the states system, imperialism, realism, idealism, levels of explanation, war and peace.

nodes.title: Introduction to Research in Political Science
nodes.description: An introduction to the design and evaluation of political research, from formulating clear questions and gathering appropriate data, to the use of simple statistical techniques for analyzing data and presenting evidence.

nodes.title: Relations Between the United States and Mexico
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: A general examination of relations between the United States and Mexico in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Emphasis on issues such as the origins of conflict and cooperation, and current issue areas including immigration.

nodes.title: POLITICS IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: A comparative analysis of the political system of a selected number of African, Asian and Middle Eastern countries, with particular development and modernization common to all of them.

nodes.title: Elementary Portuguese I
nodes.description: Beginning course in Portuguese establishing fundamental auditory and oral skills, with secondary practice in reading and writing, pronunciation, intensive oral practice. Includes laboratory work.

nodes.title: Elementary Portuguese II
nodes.prereq_text: Portuguese 1, or Portuguese 16A, with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Continues activities commenced with Portuguese 1.

nodes.title: Elementary Portuguese III
nodes.prereq_text: Portuguese 2 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Completes the basic study of the elements of the language.

nodes.title: Intermediate Portuguese
nodes.prereq_text: Portuguese 3 or Portuguese 16B, either class must be passed with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Begins review of basic grammar and syntax.

nodes.title: Intermediate Portuguese
nodes.prereq_text: Portuguese 4 with a grade of P, or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Continues review of basic grammar and syntax.

nodes.title: Intermediate Portuguese
nodes.prereq_text: Portuguese 5 with a grade of P, or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: An intensive course designed to develop students' skills in reading and oral and written expression by reading and discussing Luso-Brazilian texts and writing compositions on related topics.

nodes.title: Portuguese for Spanish Speakers
nodes.description: An intensive introductory sequence in Portuguese covering the first full year of Portuguese grammar and also advanced readings in Portuguese. Uses the grammatical structures of the Romance languages, especially Spanish, as a point of departure. Proficiency in all areas of Portuguese (reading, writing, listening, and speaking) are emphasized.

nodes.title: Portuguese for Spanish Speakers II
nodes.prereq_text: Portuguese 16A with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Intensive introductory sequence in Portuguese covering the first full year of Portuguese grammar and advanced readings in Portuguese. Uses grammatical structures of the Romance languages, especially Spanish, as point of departure. Proficiency in all areas of Portuguese (reading, writing, listening, speaking) are emphasized.

nodes.title: Advanced Grammar and Composition
nodes.description: Study of the finer points of Portuguese grammar and syntax. Equal stress is placed on written and oral practice of the language. The work in class will consist of careful study of essays and articles.

nodes.title: Survey of Portuguese Literature from the Middle Ages to the Present
nodes.description: A survey of the main writers of Portuguese Literature from its beginnings up to the present. Designed to give the student historical, cultural and literary contexts, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for understanding these contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest.

nodes.title: Survey of Portuguese Literature from the Middle Ages to the Present
nodes.description: A survey of the main writers of Portuguese Literature from its beginnings up to the present. Designed to give the student historical, cultural and literary contexts, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for understanding these contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Survey of Brazilian Literature from its Beginnings to the Present
nodes.description: A survey of the main works of literature produced in Brazil and about Brazil from its beginnings up to the present. Involves travel literature about Brazil, written in the sixteenth century, at the time of its discovery, as well as the literature produced in Brazil up to the present, represented by significant authors and periods. Designed to give the student a historical, cultural and literary context, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for the understanding of cultural contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest.

nodes.title: Survey of Brazilian Literature from its Beginnings to the Present
nodes.description: A survey of the main works of literature produced in Brazil and about Brazil from its beginnings up to the present. Involves travel literature about Brazil, written in the sixteenth century, at the time of its discovery, as well as the literature produced in Brazil up to the present, represented by significant authors and periods. Designed to give the student a historical, cultural and literary context, a chronological panel, in order to prepare the student for more specific and focused courses within the area of Portuguese. Also prepares the student for the understanding of cultural contexts in order to apply the knowledge acquired in this survey to other fields of interest. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Artistic and Interdisciplinary Approaches to Portuguese Language Countries
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: The distinctive features of Portugal, Brazil, and African countries as manifested in institutions, art, music, and literature. Taught in English

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES

nodes.title: Latino Religious Thought
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Examination of the indigenous, Iberian and North American sources and influences for distinctly Latino forms of religious thought, speculation, and spiritual construction. Topics include: Nahua wisdom traditions, colonial Nepantla, Chicano movement indigenismo, feminist innovation, Latino liberationist theology.

nodes.title: Sociology of Race and Ethnicity
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Patterns of racial and ethnic relations, with particular emphasis upon minorities in the United States.

nodes.title: Globalization and Resistance
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Examines current debates about the impact of globalization on political- economic, social, and cultural arrangements around the world, investigating how people are affected by it, and what forms resistance to these developments is taking in the emerging anti-globalization movements.

nodes.title: Development and Social Change in Latin America
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Examines significant instances of economic, political, cultural, and social change in contemporary Latin America. Employs various perspectives to illuminate such phenomena as changing social structures, industrialization, social movements, the states, multinationals, the military, and international pressures.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES

nodes.title: The Chicano Community
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Origins of the Chicano in rural Mexico; context of contact, patterns of settlement in the United States; the Chicano community, social structure, and social change; acculturation and generational patterns; community leadership and change.

nodes.title: Chicanas and Mexican Women in Contemporary Society
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Examines existing research on native-born and immigrant Mexican women in the United States with emphasis on family, education, employment, and politics. Analysis of the Chicana experience organized by considering how interplay between class, race, and gender affects access to opportunity and equality.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice and Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-mid level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: SPAN 1HY is the first course in a three-part hybrid Spanish series (SPAN 1HY, 2HY, 3HY), equivalent to the SPAN 1, 2, 3 Elementary Spanish sequence. Combining face-to-face instruction with online work, this course uses a communicative approach to develop basic Spanish skills for real-life situations. Class time focuses on active communication, with 99% of instruction conducted in Spanish. Students will build foundational grammar skills and gain insight into the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. By the end of the course, students are expected to reach Novice-Mid proficiency.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 or Spanish W1 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice and Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-high level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 or Spanish 1HY with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN 2HY is the second of the three Hybrid Elementary Spanish courses. Its hybrid format combines increased individual work with the online textbook, materials, and other web-based activities with reduced face-to-face class time and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in SPAN 2. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 2 or Spanish W2 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice; Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-high or Intermediate-low level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Completion of Spanish 2 or Spanish 2HY with a grade of P, or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN 3HY is the third of the three Hybrid Elementary Spanish courses. Its hybrid format combines increased individual work with the online textbook, materials, and other web-based activities with reduced face-to-face class time and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in SPAN 3. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish I
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 3, Spanish 3SS, 3HY, with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Language & Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Begins review of basic grammar and syntax.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 4 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Language and Culture Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Continues the review of basic grammar and syntax. Course conducted in Spanish.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 5 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Language and Culture Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Literature Examination; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: An intensive course designed to develop students' skills in reading, oral, and written expression by reading and discussing Hispanic texts, and writing compositions on related topics.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.prereq_text: Instructor or department approval required to finalize enrollment.
nodes.description: SPAN 15 is designed for students who learned Spanish at home or as a first language and provides them with the language and learning skills required to successfully complete more advanced Spanish courses (SPAN 16A/B). It focuses on formal Spanish, grammar, and reading with an emphasis on writing and vocabulary building. Students will develop awareness of linguistic registers, and practice formal speaking and writing skills through readings and discussions based on Hispanic topics in the United States and other Spanish-speaking countries. Special attention will be paid to those aspects that Spanish speakers in the United States find most problematic.

nodes.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.description: Addresses on a university level the needs and strengths of students with Spanish speaking background but no formal language training in Spanish speaking countries. Emphasizes skill in composition, advanced reading comprehension, standard versus vernacular usages, cross language interference, etc.

nodes.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 16A with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Addresses on university level the needs and strengths of students with Spanish speaking background but no formal language training in Spanish speaking countries. Emphasizes more complex skills in composition and advanced reading comprehension than Spanish 16A, as well as standard versus vernacular usages, cross language interferences, etc.

nodes.title: Advanced Grammar and Composition
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 6 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 4 or 5 on the AP Spanish Literature Examination; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Intensive course taught in Spanish designed to reinforce students' comprehension and ability to express themselves in Spanish, both orally and in writing, and to develop the students' vocabularies and awareness of syntactical structures in the language.

nodes.title: Soccer in the Hispanic World
nodes.description: This course approaches soccer as a cultural phenomenon to examine its historical development, social meanings, and role in articulating national identities and experiences of displacement across the Hispanic world. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Culture and Revolution in the Americas
nodes.description: What is a revolution? What do art and literature tell us about revolutionary movements and the hopes, promises, and memories associated with them? This course will examine these questions focusing on some of the major revolutionary episodes in the history of the Americas: the Haitian Revolution (1791-1804), the Wars of Independence in Spanish America (1810-1824), the Mexican Revolution (1910-1920), and the Cuban Revolution (1959). Through the analysis of artistic and literary pieces across various genres and media, we will delve into topics such as identity, liberty, governance, legitimacy, violence, trauma, and the construction of history. Taught in English. There may be a discussion section in Spanish depending on the enrollment.

nodes.title: The US/México Border
nodes.description: The class purpose is to survey the Mexico/U.S border regions cultural production of the past century. It pays special attention to aesthetic and ideological discourses that nurture artistic and political ties required to resist state violence at and across the U.S.-Mexico border. It takes an interdisciplinary approach to understand the sociopolitical realities of the most populated merging points between Latin America and the United States. Material includes readings from different disciplines as well as cultural productions: film, visual arts, literature, music, podcasts and performance art to offer a rich and diverse examination of cultural manifestations and socio-political movements from a transborder perspective. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Introduction to Hispanic Linguistics
nodes.prereq_text: SPAN 16B or SPAN 25 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introduction to linguistic theories, methods, and problems as applied to Spanish. Taught in Spanish with Spanish examples.

nodes.title: Advanced Composition through Literature
nodes.description: The study of the finer points of Spanish grammar and syntax. Stress is placed on writing critical analyses of literary readings.

nodes.title: Advanced Composition through Literature
nodes.description: The study of the finer points of Spanish grammar and syntax. Stress is placed on writing critical analyses of literary readings.

nodes.title: Beyond Advanced Spanish Proficiency
nodes.description: Designed to provide students who have completed Span 25 or Span 16B and one additional upper-division Spanish course with the opportunity to practice the four language skills: speaking, listening, reading, and writing. Students will practice different communicative skills, from defending an opinion to mastering transactions and exchanges.

nodes.title: Teaching Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.description: Designed for students who have completed Span 100 and who are considering a teaching career. The course covers frequent issues encountered when working with students who have learned Spanish through their family history or place of origin.

nodes.title: Spanish in the United States: The Language and Its Speakers
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Study of Spanish used in United States by native and immigrant groups: Mexicans, Chicanos, Cubans, Puerto Ricans and others in Spanish-speaking enclaves. Focus on language and social and cultural manifestations arising in contact between linguistically different groups. Taught in Spanish.

nodes.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Medieval Spanish literature.

nodes.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Golden age literature.

nodes.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Spanish literature.

nodes.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Twentieth-century Spanish literature.

nodes.title: Spanish-American Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Colonial Spanish-American literature.

nodes.title: Spanish-American Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Nineteenth-century Spanish-American literature.

nodes.title: Spanish-American Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Twentieth-century Spanish-American literature.

nodes.title: Introduction to Translation I
nodes.description: Comprises topics necessary to develop skills that are needed for writing at a specialized level and to carry out written translation into and from Spanish, mostly texts on business and medical topics.

nodes.title: Introduction to Interpreting
nodes.prereq_text: SPAN 16B or SPAN 25 (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for interpretation to and from Spanish. Intended mostly for proficient Spanish-language speakers.

nodes.title: Specialized Translation - Legal
nodes.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for writing at a specialized level, and with specialized vocabulary, for the legal profession.

nodes.title: Specialized Translation - Technical
nodes.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for writing at a specialized level, and with specialized vocabulary and format, for the translation of different types of technical texts (instruction manuals, medical, patents, etc.).

nodes.title: Spanish Institutions and Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Study of the development of the Spanish nation, with special focus on key social and political institutions, the arts and major currents of thought.

nodes.title: Spanish Cinema
nodes.description: Introduces twentieth-century Spain through significant films, analyzing how cinema represents social, political, and cultural issues, as well as key themes, genres, and filmmakers.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES

nodes.title: The Fantastic and Its Development in Spanish-American Short Story
nodes.description: Exploration of the multiple manifestations of the Fantastic in Spanish American short story from its origin, linked to nineteenth-century sensationalistic journalism, up to neofantastic mode appearing circa 1950, with its more epistemological goals.

nodes.title: Spanish Golden Age Poetry I
nodes.description: Lyric poetry of the sixteenth century: Garcilaso, Luis de Leon, San Juan de La Cruz, and others.

nodes.title: Modern Mexican Literature
nodes.description: Study of texts explaining the development of Mexican culture and literature. Topic and writers: modernism (from Gutierrez Najera to Tablada); the novel of the Mexican revolution (Azuela); and the modern essay (Alfonso Reyes and Octavio Paz).

nodes.title: Golden Age Drama
nodes.description: The classic comedia, by Lope, Tirso, Alarcon, Calderon, and other dramatists.

nodes.title: Golden Age Drama
nodes.description: The classic comedia, by Lope, Tirso, Alarcon, Calderon, and other dramatists.

nodes.title: Contemporary Mexican Literature
nodes.description: Continued study of major trends in Mexican literature as evidenced in selected works of the following authors: the poetry of Lopez Velarde and Octavio Paz; the contemporaneos (Torres Bodet, Villaurrutia, Pellicer); and contemporary fiction (Yanez, Rulfo, Arreola, and Fuentes).

nodes.title: Cervantes: Don Quijote
nodes.description: Reading and discussion of the first and second parts of Don Quixote.

nodes.title: Contemporary Indigenous Cultures of Mexico
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Examines the work of writers that have recently provided increased visibility to indigenous languages and cultures in contemporary Mexico, including Nahuatl, Zapotec, and Mayan.

nodes.title: Culture and Crisis
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Traces the ways in which literature represents crisis in different moments of the Spanish history. The course focuses on fundamental concepts like historical memory, bio politics, insecurity and anti-austerity movements in Contemporary Spain.

nodes.title: Business Spanish
nodes.description: Real-life situations in the workplace will present students with the appropriate vocabulary for business environments. Students learn to write formal documents, how to express themselves orally, and to assess the business environment of different Spanish-speaking countries from a cultural perspective.

nodes.title: Soccer: The Cultural Impact of a Global Game
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Soccer is a mirror of our world and an expression of our greatest tragedies and hopes.Thiscourse seeks to use soccer as a tool for learning about politics, economics, culture, society, philosophy, art, literature andthe human condition in the Hispanic world.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES

nodes.title: Barcelona: The Making of an Urban Landscape
nodes.description: Explores the rich history and cultural evolution of Barcelona, one of the most iconic cities in the world. From its humble beginnings as a Roman colony to its current status as a bustling cosmopolitan city, Barcelona has undergone numerous transformations throughout its history. Through a multidisciplinary approach, which includes a combination of films, readings, and other visual materials, we delve into the construction of Barcelona as a modern metropolis and trace the ways in which its cultural legacies are still present in its urban landscape today.

nodes.title: Basque Studies
nodes.description: An overview of the cultural and historical characteristics of the Basque Country while analyzing how minoritized groups, such as the Basque, negotiate their identity in the face of globalization.

nodes.title: Basque Studies
nodes.description: An overview of the cultural and historical characteristics of the Basque Country while analyzing how minoritized groups, such as the Basque, negotiate their identity in the face of globalization. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Basque Language and Culture
nodes.description: An intensive course for students with no previous study of the Basque language.

nodes.title: Basque Language and Culture
nodes.description: Continues activities commenced in Spanish 154A.

nodes.title: Basque Language and Culture
nodes.description: Continues activities commenced in SPAN 154A and SPAN 154B.

nodes.title: Discourses of Love and Desire: from The Book of Good Love to the Present
nodes.description: This course sequence (SPAN 155 A - B) traces the literary constructions, elaborations, and treatments of love in Spanish literature from Middle Ages to the present. SPAN 155A (Pre-1700) focuses specifically on the development of courtly love and neoplatonic visions of love in the Iberian Peninsula as they pertain to a variety of literary and cultural forms.

nodes.title: Discourses of Love and Desire: from The Book of Good Love to the Present
nodes.description: This course sequence (SPAN 155 A - B) traces the literary constructions, elaborations, and treatments of love in Spanish literature from Middle Ages to the present. SPAN 155B (Post- 1700) explores the psychological and sociological implications and the cultural significance of love in a variety of art forms, poetry, drama, novel and film.

nodes.title: Introduction to Galician Studies
nodes.description: The uniqueness of the culture and language of Galicia, its history, ethnography, folklore, and literature, in Galician and Spanish.

nodes.title: Nicaraguan Poetry
nodes.description: Surveys the poetry of Nicaragua from its origins to the present. It frames key authors and representative poetic texts within their literary and cultural context. Poets include Daro, Corts, Selva, Cuadra, and Belli.

nodes.title: Posmodernismo
nodes.description: Study of the Spanish and Spanish-American Postmodernistas, exploring the link between the culture of modernity and the emergence of a colloquial, prosaic, but lyrical discourse in late nineteenth and twentieth century Spanish and Spanish-American poetry.

nodes.title: Literature and Cultural Identity in the Spanish Caribbean
nodes.description: Survey of Spanish Caribbean literature from the standpoint of interaction of culture and race. It traces the counterpoint among the diverse ethnic groups that populate the Caribbean and the manner in which the discourse ofthe oppressor and the oppressed intertwine.

nodes.title: Contemporary Spanish Cultural Studies
nodes.description: An interdisciplinary approach to the understanding of present-day Spain, focusing on popular music, TV and literature from the 1960s until today.

nodes.title: Spanish-American Thought
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Leading social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends from the sixteenth century to the present.

nodes.title: Mexican Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Area A: SOCIAL SCIENCES
nodes.description: Social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends in the developmentof modern Mexico.

nodes.title: Hispanic Poetry: 1900 to 1945
nodes.description: Reading and discussion of twentieth-century Spanish and Spanish-American poets and trends in their socio-historical context.

nodes.title: Contemporary Spanish-American Short Story
nodes.description: A study of the trends, themes and techniques of the contemporary Spanish American short story with emphasis on major authors such as Borges, Cortzar, Ocampo, Onetti, Rulfo, Carpentier, Garca Mrquez, and others.

nodes.title: The Spanish-American Nueva Novela
nodes.description: Readings of such authors as Borges, Rulfo Fuentes, Vargas Llosa, Garcia Marquez, Donoso. Emphasis put on the innovative structure and language brought to Hispanic literature by the so-called Nueva Novela.

nodes.title: Modern Hispanic Drama
nodes.description: Representative dramatists of Spain such as Unamuno, Valle-Inclan, Garcia Lorca, Buero Vallejo, and others.

nodes.title: Modernismo
nodes.description: Introduction to the poetry and prose of Hispanic Modernismo. Major writers and their most representative works: Marti, Dario, Rodo, Lugones. Lyric poetry, short story, novel, the essay, and other forms are studied.

nodes.title: Borges and His Precursors
nodes.description: This course focuses on Borges the Reader, and traces in particular his affinities with North American and European literatures.

nodes.title: Independent Studies in Spanish
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Spanish and consent of department.

items.text: completion of two upper-division courses in Spanish

nodes.description: Independent studies in selected subjects not covered by course offerings.

nodes.title: Online Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: Span W1 is the first course of the Elementary Spanish three course sequence delivered in a fully online format. By the end of this course students are expected to develop basic proficiency in Spanish at the Novice-mid level.

nodes.title: Online Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN W 2 is the second of the three Elementary Spanish courses offered in a fully online format. Its online format combines technology-based language instruction with online class meetings and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in the regular Elementary Span II course. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. Each week, students attend one online class session and one conversation session. There is individual work with the textbook, online materials, and other web-based activities.
